detail.title: Synthesis of Institutional Filtering and Observer Disagreement
detail.summary: This research entry synthesizes findings on how observers study the same subject while reaching divergent conclusions. Analysis of existing evidence suggests that institutional constraints, historical geography, and local decision-making frameworks function as predictive filters, structuring the information available to an observer. Rather than simple subjective bias, observer disagreement emerges as a structural consequence of how specific institutional contexts prioritize and organize input. The provisional notebook nb-observer-disag-synth-001 details these mechanisms, linking historical geography and electoral decision models to support the claim that institutional environments materially condition expert consensus.
